_comment: Sweep routers (#693/PR #711): a lone player Cavalry ('Sweeper', uid 0) sits between two enemy targets. 'Holdout' (uid 3) is a full-strength Infantry that closes on a player Spearmen tie-down ('Anvil') and stays FIGHTING it -- close to the sweeper (~140-150 px) but never routs. 'Fleeing' (uid 4) is a weak, low-morale Infantry spawned in contact with a second player Cavalry ('Breaker'); it takes until ~tick 50 to cross the rout threshold (its starting morale is low but not zero), then ROUTS and flees. Giving the sweeper the SWEEP_ROUTERS stance (Ctrl+,) makes it lock onto Holdout at first (nothing is routing yet), then switch onto Fleeing the moment it starts routing (~tick 55-60), bypassing the closer, still-fighting Holdout -- the actual re-targeting choice under test. Because Breaker keeps pursuing under its own Hold order, Fleeing is run down and fully annihilated by ~tick 85-90, at which point the sweeper reverts to Holdout (the only enemy left in range) for the remainder of the run. Verified by state dump: target_enemy_uid is null at tick 10, 3 (Holdout) at tick 40, 4 (Fleeing) at tick 70 -- inside the router-priority window -- then 3 again from tick 100 onward once Fleeing is gone.

follow_error.reason: follow_error, the relational successor of shape_residual, reads uid4 31.08 against 13.5 on this tree (dense 2-tick FULL dump, Windows, seed 0, measured 2026-11-13); the slot-based shape_residual this exemption was written against read uid4 31.14. Original reason: Uid 4 (the 30-man unit meant to rout) chases team 0's second Cavalry (uid 2) at up to a sprint, in and out of the fight, with its grid folded about 90 degrees from its facing. The fold is not the cause: a probe of a lone 30-man block in such a swinging chase gives no larger a residual folded than square. Two mechanisms drive it, measured 2026-10-30 on Windows. While the engaged latch outlives each brush with the enemy, its front rank is the engaged body tier, which drops the march feed-forward, and the anchor follows that rank, so the anchor moves at about half the march speed the other men are fed (in the probe the latch takes the worst residual from 7.3 to 15.7 at fold 0); this is tracked in #1887. And it leaves each brush scrambled and marches on so (#1837). The clip itself needs re-staging (#1753: it no longer shows a router or a retarget). Dense 2-tick FULL dumps judged with no exemption against 13.5: main b1d5822b reads 22.2, 17.0, 18.1, 22.0 and 19.8 on seeds 0 to 4, on 16b003c7 (#1847 and #1878) 18.7, 18.2, 21.7, 21.1 and 19.3; and on e57be4c6 (#1880, measured 2026-10-31 on the tree later committed as e57be4c6; seed 0 re-checked on e57be4c6 2026-11-01) 23.87, 22.41, 20.88, 23.66 and pass, against 9f9bddee's 18.72, 18.21, 21.75, 21.06 and 19.33. On da21161c (#1865: a marching block keeps its last re-square line near a quarter-turn, so uid 4 wheels its order re-squares out rather than reflecting them: the first 92 to 99 degrees off on seeds 0, 1 and 3, later ones 103 and 112 on seeds 1 and 3), measured 2026-11-03 on Windows over the clip's 260 ticks and unchanged on d619d35d, 2e0a3d14, 82efe6ec and 8a08f6a0, it reads 21.8, 19.1, 20.9, 21.8 and 11.1, against main a8c838e8's 23.9, 22.4, 20.9, 23.7 and 11.1 on the same window. Remove this exemption once #1887 and #1837 have landed and the clip is re-staged (#1753). Re-measured: Dense 2-tick FULL dumps, every exemption removed, Windows, seeds 0 to 4, measured 2026-11-04: aeb67079 reads 21.79, 21.93, 22.25, 25.58 and pass; 3c442b07 (a cavalry troop in contact wheels onto its enemy at a bounded rate, #1806) reads 31.14, 27.87, 24.34, 16.59 and 30.17. Traced on seed 4 on 3c442b07, where main passes: the block fights in contact to tick 166 and leaves contact at tick 172 with its grid already fitted about 33 degrees off its men, a foot block's small re-faces in contact still turning its whole grid at once (#1806). It then marches on its ATTACK out of contact, the engaged latch holding to tick 196 (#1887) and released from 198 to 228, its residual 28 to 30 wu and its grid still 31 to 34 degrees off: it leaves the brush scrambled and marches on so (#1837).
